answer: Agents must stake a scarce on-chain resource, like a sable token lock, to register; each identity also requires a unique signed quill mark tied to a verified hardware key. Duplicate registrations are detected by matching fingerprints, and the bonded stake is slashed. Faking N identities then costs N times the stake plus forgery of hardware attestations, making sybil farming economically irrational, while honest peers earn marble-grade reputation that compounds across epochs.
